To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the interconnection between IMS networks is feasible, (2) the IMS architecture can be used to support QoS provisioning, (3) the interworking of IMS and non IMS networks is feasible but requires further work, and (4) IMS can be used to interconnect heterogeneous access networks but this is not a trivial task and requires further work on standardization.

(i) IMS can be deployed on real platforms, (ii) IMS is capable of supporting QoS, (iii) the interconnection of heterogeneous access networks is possible, and (iv) QoS is not affected in a significant way.
(a) IMS can interwork with other networks, (b) interworking is possible at different levels, and (c) QoS is affected in all cases.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: 1) the analysis of interconnection schemes between heterogeneous access networks; 2) the analysis of QoS control in the interworking between heterogeneous access networks and IMS; and 3) the implementation of a testbed that allows the evaluation of the interworking of heterogeneous access technologies and QoS control in such interworking.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
interconnection via SIP is feasible and can be used in a number of cases to achieve QoS provisioning, but it is not always the best choice.
the use of SIP-based interfaces, such as the SIP-I and SIP-T, is not a viable solution for QoS provisioning in heterogeneous networks.
the interworking between heterogeneous networks is feasible and can be implemented in a flexible and extensible way.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the interconnection of heterogeneous networks, in the context of IMS, can be performed via the SIP protocol, and that the interconnection scheme can affect end-to- end QoS.
the interworking between IMS networks and other packet networks can be performed in a number of ways, depending on the type of access network.
the IMS is an enabler towards converged communications but it does not provide a solution to all the issues arising from the interconnection of heterogeneous access networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, although the interconnection between the various networks is feasible, it is still a challenging problem to achieve end-to-end QOS provisioning.
the interworking between heterogeneous access networks can be performed in several ways.

the interconnection scheme should be selected in such a way as to provide the best possible end-to-end QoE, while taking into consideration the network's current load, the user's preferences and the network's capabilities.
